items.stem: An AI summary states a company's quarterly revenue grew 12%. Before putting this in a client-facing note, what should the analyst do?

options.text: Trace the figure back to the primary filing and confirm the period and number
options.rationale: Correct: figures must be verified against primary sources before client use.

options.text: Publish it because the summary sounded authoritative
options.rationale: Authoritative tone does not guarantee the number is correct or current.

options.text: Round it up to make the story stronger
options.rationale: Altering figures to improve a narrative is misleading and improper.

options.text: Assume the model never makes numerical errors
options.rationale: Models can misstate or carry stale figures; verification is required.

items.explanation: Correct: figures must be verified against primary sources before client use.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate uses of AI in investment research? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Drafting a first-pass summary of a long filing for an analyst to check
options.rationale: Correct: summarisation to be verified is a sound, time-saving use.

options.text: Generating scenario questions to structure an analyst's own thinking
options.rationale: Correct: AI can help frame scenarios the analyst then evaluates.

options.text: Issuing an automated buy recommendation directly to clients with no review
options.rationale: Unreviewed AI recommendations to clients carry serious compliance and accuracy risk.

options.text: Fabricating figures when the source is unavailable

items.explanation: Correct: summarisation to be verified is a sound, time-saving use.

items.stem: An analyst presents an AI-generated two-scenario comparison to the portfolio manager as 'what will happen' to a stock. Why is this framing wrong?

options.text: Scenarios are illustrative assumptions, not predictions of actual outcomes
options.rationale: Correct: scenario outputs rest on assumptions and must not be sold as forecasts.

options.text: AI scenarios are always exactly correct
options.rationale: Scenarios depend on assumptions and are not guaranteed outcomes.

options.text: Portfolio managers cannot read scenario analysis
options.rationale: PMs use scenarios routinely; the issue is the misleading framing.

options.text: Comparisons should never be shown to a PM
options.rationale: Comparisons are useful when framed honestly as scenarios.

items.explanation: Correct: scenario outputs rest on assumptions and must not be sold as forecasts.
